subject: Discovery recap + POC data collection & evaluation plan
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@sparrowtech.com>, SparrowTech POC <poc@sparrowtech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T14:10:00-04:00
Subject: Discovery recap + next steps (POC data)

Hi Liam / SparrowTech team,

Thanks again for the productive call earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC kickoff:

- Goal: Validate that Redwood can meet SparrowTech's real-time summarization SLA (95th pctile < 400ms) and keep inference spend under $0.0015/token on average for your 1M-month token profile.
- Success criteria (prelim): latency SLO as above, >= 92% ROUGE-based summary adequacy on the eval set, and no data egress outside your VPC during Private deployment testing.
- Data we need from you for a representative trial: a) a 1-2 week anonymized prompt/log export (max 10k prompts) that reflects the highest-throughput flows, b) any existing evaluation prompts or labeled summaries (if available).
- Timeline: aim to start data ingest and baseline runs w/c 2026-08-24, 2-week trial window, then a 1-week results review.
- Owners: Camila (sales) will coordinate logistics; Rishi (solutions) will own evaluation runs and config; Marissa (customer success) will own rollout playbook and success criteria sign-off.

Please confirm: 1) who will upload the prompt/log export and when, 2) whether the privacy team needs an NDA amendment for logs, 3) any non-negotiable security controls we should include in the baseline run (e.g., HSM/KMS restrictions).

I've attached a lightweight template for the eval plan (redwood_poc_eval_template.xlsx) and a sampling guidance doc. If you can share the export as JSONL (one prompt per line) that makes ingestion straightforward.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20-min sync if useful.

— Camila
Camila Reyes | Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_poc_eval_template.xlsx (Excel, 48 KB)]
[Attachment: sampling_guidance.md (Markdown, 6 KB)]

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@sparrowtech.com>

Cc: SparrowTech POC <poc@sparrowtech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T17:02:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + next steps (POC data)

Hi Camila — thanks for the clear recap. Quick responses below:

- We'll provide an anonymized export of prompts and the last 30 days of request logs. I expect the team can prepare a JSONL export by EOD 2026-08-18. The export will include: timestamp, user_locale (redacted), prompt_text, and contextual metadata fields (flow_id, product_area).
- Success criteria: those numbers look reasonable. We would suggest adding a qualitative check: manual assessment of 100 sampled summaries for business-meaning preservation. If we hit 92% ROUGE but summaries miss key legal clauses, that would fail for us.
- Security: we need the Private deployment option for the trial (VPC + KMS). Our security team will need the runbook and proof of no external egress.

I've looped in our POC mailbox and legal contact separately off-thread for the NDA amendment.

We'll upload the export to the Drive link you provided (or you can enable a secure SFTP if that's easier).

— Liam
Liam O'Connor | Head of Platform | SparrowTech

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@sparrowtech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-13T09:18:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + next steps (POC data)

Thanks — stepping in on the technical plan side. A couple of clarifications and a suggested eval approach:

1) Data format: JSONL with fields {id, ts, prompt, meta.flow_id, meta.product_area}. Redact any PII before export. If you can include a small mapping file for flow_id -> human label that helps sampling.

2) Sampling for eval: we'll run two passes — a production-weighted pass (stratified by flow_id volume) and a stress pass (top 10% longest prompts). For each pass we'll generate N=1000 automated eval comparisons and a human-reviewed sample of 100 items per pass for qualitative assessment.

3) Metrics: latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), tokens-per-request, ROUGE-L and a proprietary 'preservation' score (0-1). We'll produce a short report and a dashboard link.

4) Ownership: Rishi will run ingestion and baseline numbers; Marissa will coordinate the 100-sample human review with your SMEs; Camila will manage stakeholder updates.

5) Timeline tweak: if upload happens by 2026-08-18 we can start ingest on 2026-08-19 and have a baseline report by 2026-08-26. Let us know if you need a slower cadence.

I'll also attach a short sampling_guidance.md that spells out the sampling code and anonymization checklist.

— Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sampling_guidance.md (Markdown, 6 KB)]

Perfect — thank you both. Quick checklist and asks before we ingest:

- Please upload the JSONL export to the Drive link by 2026-08-18 OR confirm SFTP details. Mark the file: sparrowtech_prompts_export.jsonl.
- Confirm who on your side will do the 100-sample qualitative review and provide a short rubric (we can use Marissa's template).
- Confirm NDA amendment: legal/deferred to your legal contact — if needed we can route a one-page addendum for logs-only testing.
- If you have any redaction constraints (e.g., remove legal_case_id fields), list them in the Drive README.

If everything looks good we'll treat 2026-08-19 as Day 0 for ingestion and send a short kickoff calendar invite.

Thanks — Camila
